newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke lectures Conservative MPs on the economy.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke lectures Conservative MPs on the economy.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke told a key committee of Conservative members of parliament on Wednesday that the British economy was in great shape.
Paraphrasing the rallying call for U.S. President Bill Clinton in his first election campaign, Clarke told reporters his theme to the 1922 committee was: "It's the economy stupid."

News that Clarke was addressing the highly important committee, which represents Conservative MPs who are not ministers, raised speculation that he would be grilled on the thorny issue of a single European currency.
But he said he had not talked about EMU even though the ruling Conservatives' faultline on that issue has gaped wide open again.

Early on Wednesday, Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind told BBC radio that on balance the government was "hostile" to European economic and monetary union (EMU). Clarke later dismissed the comments as a "slip of the tongue" while Prime Minister John Major said the government was unpersuaded about EMU but stressed the government's "wait and see" policy remained in place.
One MP described Clarke's address to the 1992 committee as "marvellous, straight down the line on the strength of the economy."
A less sympathetic member described it as "a lecture in A-level economics if that."
Clarke, firmly on the pro-European wing of the Conservative Party, is far from popular with the many Eurosceptics in the party.
The meeting lasted for just 20 minutes.
